messages:
maria: Heads-up — instrumented a customer flow and noticing child spans missing in traces for /api/v2/generate. Parent root span present but decoder/kv-cache/grpc-client spans are absent for a subset of requests since ~06:10 UTC. :thinking:
ingest-bot: exporter-heartbeat: collector-3 briefly lost connection to otlp-sink (06:09:52Z -> recovered 06:10:25Z).
kevin: Any chance this is sampling or sampler reconfiguration for that tenant?
maria: Sampler config unchanged. Pulled raw HTTP headers from the ingress sidecar for one of the affected requests — see below. There are two traceparent headers with same trace-id but different span-id. That would explain orphaned children.
```
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-7345f067aa0ba902b-01
```
sam: Two different span IDs under same trace — which one does otel-col prefer?
lee: The collector/propagator takes the first `traceparent` header and uses that as the parent. If upstream spans use the second header value, they won't link (parent mismatch) and show up as separate roots or be dropped by our UI grouping.
kevin: How are we ending up with duplicate traceparent headers? Envoy? NGX? SDK?
maria: Edge sidecar is nginx-based and we recently added an explicit `proxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent;` in a template. Some clients already forwarded headers and `proxy_pass_request_headers on;` was still enabled on some instances — that results in duplicate entries. Also seen with legacy SDK behavior in a few customers.
sam: Can we make collector tolerant — detect multiple headers and pick the one that matches existing spans? Might be safer in case other proxies do weird things.
lee: We can, but collector logic change is riskier and slower to rollout. Short-term fix: normalize at ingress (coalesce duplicates, choose the last or the one with a valid parent-id). I prepared a small patch to the nginx template plus a lightweight Lua filter to collapse duplicate `traceparent` headers and prefer the last occurrence.
maria: Patch link: https://redwood.internal/pull/eng/ingress/342 (canary-ready). Applying canary to edge cluster 3 now. Also adding a collector metric to count requests with multiple traceparent headers so we can monitor.
ops-bot: deploy started: ingress-edge-3 canary (06:25 UTC)
kevin: After canary, confirm traces for /api/v2/generate show children again. If that checks, rollout to remaining edges. Also create a dashboard panel for proportion of traces with duplicate traceparent header.
maria: Canary sanity check: sampled 20 traces pre-fix vs 20 post-fix — children reappeared in all post-fix samples. Rolling to rest of edges in ~15m.
sam: Opening follow-up issue: collector should log and increment a counter when multiple `traceparent` headers are seen (low cardinality metric). We'll refer to it in the postmortem.
lee: Long-term: audit all header rewrite templates and our client SDKs for duplicated propagation headers. Add QA test in infra repo that simulates duplicated headers and verifies end-to-end parent-child linking.
maria: Thanks y'all. I'll keep this thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
kevin: Nice find — good containment plan. :eyes:
